Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NovaTel Communications Q4 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NovaTel Communications' Q4 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Network Officer; David Kim, Chief Commercial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We're very pleased with our performance in the Q4, driven by strong execution and a favorable market environment. We are focused on delivering long-term sustainable growth. Our achievements include robust capital expenditure discipline supporting network investments that fuel our competitive edge. We are also seeing substantial growth from enterprise and B2B initiatives with significant key wins. Further, we are concentrating on optimizing spectrum assets for maximum utilization. Additionally, free cash flow generation is strong, enabling smart utilization. We are also improving our cost of revenue trends through efficiency gains. We are strategically investing in subscriber and revenue expansion plans. Finally, dividend sustainability remains a priority alongside shareholder returns.

Mike Chen: Thank you, Alex. Moving to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $15.4 billion, representing a 4% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA was $6.5 billion, resulting in a margin of 42%. We continue to manage our expenses prudently and are optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures were $3.3 billion, primarily focused on expanding our 5G network and fiber infrastructure.

As we wrap up another strong year, I'd like to dive deep into our capital expenditure—or capex—guidance, with a particular focus on network investments, which remain the bedrock of our competitive moat in the hyper-competitive telecom and media landscape. Network capex isn't just about spending; it's about fueling sustainable revenue growth, enhancing customer experience, and positioning us for the next wave of connectivity-driven media consumption.

Over the past three years, we've methodically ramped network investments to accelerate our 5G standalone deployment and fiber-to-the-home footprint, responding to surging data demand from 5G smartphones, 4K/8K streaming, cloud gaming, and enterprise edge computing. FY2022 network capex was $7.8 billion, representing 18% of our total revenue of $43 billion. That climbed to $8.9 billion in FY2023, or 17% of $52 billion revenue, as we prioritized C-band spectrum deployment following our $3.2 billion FCC auction win in 2022, much like AT&T and Verizon. For FY2024, we delivered on our guidance with $9.4 billion in network capex—down slightly to 16% of our record $59 billion revenue—thanks to improved capex efficiency from Open RAN trials and AI-optimized supply chains.

This discipline has driven tangible results: our 5G SA coverage now reaches 92% of our North American postpaid base, up from 65% last year, boosting ARPU by 4.2% year-over-year through premium unlimited plans bundled with our NovaStream media service. Wireline fiber passings grew 22% to 28 million homes, reducing churn to 0.9% and supporting symmetrical gigabit speeds that power our competitive edge against cable peers like Comcast.

Turning to FY2025 guidance: We're raising the bar with total capex of $13.2 billion to $13.8 billion, flat as a percentage of projected revenue growth to $64-$66 billion. Of this, network investments will total $10.2 billion to $10.6 billion, up 8-13% year-over-year, reflecting our commitment to outpacing industry averages per Dell'Oro Group estimates of 5-7% sector growth. This guidance assumes no major macroeconomic shocks, stable inflation at 2-3%, and continued supply chain resilience post the 2024 chip shortage.

Breaking it down by category for transparency: Wireless network gets $6.1-$6.4 billion, or 60% of network capex. This funds the final push to 98% 5G SA coverage in the US and Canada, including mid-band C-band densification in high-traffic urban corridors like the Northeast Megalopolis and Southern California. We'll deploy 15,000 additional massive MIMO sites with Ericsson's RAN portfolio, emphasizing virtualized RAN for 25% opex savings long-term. In Europe, via our Vodafone JV, $1.2 billion targets sub-1GHz low-band refarming to counter aggressive pricing from Iliad and 1&1. Asia-Pacific expansion—our fastest-growing region at 15% sub revenue CAGR—gets $800 million for mmWave small cells in Singapore and Indonesia, partnering with Nokia for disaggregated Open RAN to support our 5G fixed wireless access ramp, now serving 2.5 million households.

Wireline and fiber: $2.8-$3.0 billion, or 28%. Building on XGS-PON momentum, we'll pass an additional 6-7 million locations, prioritizing greenfield builds in underserved US Sunbelt markets like Texas and Florida and rural broadband via BEAD funding—expecting $1.1 billion in grants matching our $2.2 billion investment. This counters satellite threats like Starlink, where our fiber delivers 70% lower latency for media pros like live sports streaming on our NovaStream platform.

Media and edge infrastructure: $1.3-$1.2 billion, or 12%. Here, we're future-proofing for the streaming wars. $700 million expands our content delivery network with 200 new edge POPs, integrating AWS Outposts for low-latency delivery of 4K HDR content—critical as our NovaStream subs hit 45 million, driving 18% year-over-year ad revenue growth. Another $500 million invests in AI/ML orchestration for dynamic spectrum sharing and predictive maintenance, reducing network downtime to under 0.01% and enabling new services like AR/VR metaverse experiences.

Regionally, North America commands 65% of the spend at $6.6-$6.9 billion, fueled by 6GHz spectrum advocacy and enterprise 5G private networks for media clients like Disney and Netflix. EMEA at 20%, or $2.0-$2.1 billion, focuses on regulatory tailwinds from the EU's Gigabit Society goals, while APAC/LATAM at 15%, or $1.6 billion, leverages partnerships like our Reliance Jio tie-up in India for JioFiber synergies.

Strategically, this capex profile underscores our 'efficient growth' thesis: intensity dips to 15.5-16% of revenue from 16% in FY2024, thanks to 20% faster deployment cycles via automation and modular designs. ROI metrics are robust—5G capex is yielding 2.5x EBITDA multiples within 24 months, per our internal models, outpacing 4G. We're also R&D-seeding 6G with $200 million, collaborating with Qualcomm and NTT DoCoMo on terahertz trials.

Risks include supply chain volatility from TSMC dependencies and potential FCC auction delays, but our $4.5 billion cash pile and 2.1x net debt/EBITDA provide ample dry powder. We expect this investment to deliver 300-400 bps EBITDA margin expansion to 42-43% by FY2027.

Before we move on, let me provide our forward-looking guidance for Q1 FY2025 and full-year FY2025, with some color on the key drivers. NovaTel operates at the intersection of telecommunications and media, with our three core segments—Wireless, Wireline Broadband, and NovaStream OTT—delivering integrated connectivity and content solutions to over 120 million subscribers globally.

Starting with subscriber growth guidance. We continue to see robust momentum across our portfolio, fueled by our aggressive 5G SA rollout, FTTH expansion, and bundling strategies that lock in multi-product households. For Q1 FY2025, we guide to total subscriber net adds of 1.8 million, representing approximately 1.5% quarter-over-quarter growth. Wireless postpaid subscribers: +1.2 million net adds, up 1.8% QoQ, driven by our 5G Ultra Wideband network now covering 95% of our top 100 U.S. markets and strong uptake of our Unlimited Ultimate plans, which include bundled NovaStream access. This compares favorably to T-Mobile's recent postpaid phone net adds, as our ARPU premiumization—now at $58.50, up 4% YoY—offsets any promotional intensity.

Wireline broadband: +450,000 net adds, up 3.2% QoQ, primarily from FTTH deployments reaching 2.5 million new locations in the quarter. We're outpacing Comcast Xfinity in gigabit-tier adoption, with 65% of new broadband subs opting for 1Gbps+ speeds, supported by our capex ramp in the Northeast and Southeast U.S.

NovaStream OTT: +150,000 net adds, up 2.1% QoQ, bolstered by exclusive content deals like our multi-year partnership with Lionsgate for premium originals and live sports FAST channels, which have reduced churn to 1.2% monthly—below Netflix's reported SVOD averages.

For the full FY2025, we now guide to total subscriber growth of 7.8% YoY, or approximately 8.2 million net adds, up from our prior guide of 7.5% due to better-than-expected 5G device attach rates, now 55% of our base, and international expansion in Latin America via our JV with Claro in Mexico and Brazil, where we're adding 500,000 prepaid-to-postpaid conversions annually.

Turning to revenue growth guidance. We expect Q1 FY2025 total revenue of $15.4 billion to $15.6 billion, implying 3% to 4% YoY growth and a 2.5% QoQ increase. Wireless: $9.8 billion, up 4% YoY, with service revenue growth of 5% driven by 3% price adjustments on mid-tier plans, implemented mid-Q4 with minimal pushback, netting +$1.20 ARPU uplift, and equipment sales stabilization at $2.1 billion amid iPhone 16 cycle demand. Enterprise 5G private networks, like our deal with Ford for connected vehicle slicing, contribute $150 million incrementally.

Wireline Broadband: $3.7 billion, up 6% YoY, led by 8% growth in high-margin FTTH revenue at $1.2 billion, as we hit 40% FTTH penetration in our footprint—mirroring Charter's Spectrum momentum but with superior EBITDA margins at 52%.

NovaStream: $1.0 billion, up 2% YoY, with advertising revenue surging 15% to $350 million on targeted AVOD tiers, offsetting modest SVOD pricing pressure in a competitive landscape with Disney+ and Paramount+.

For full FY2025, revenue guidance is raised to $64 billion to $66 billion, or 7% to 7.5% YoY growth, ahead of consensus. This reflects total service revenue expansion of 8% to around $52 billion, with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding 100bps to 42%, supported by opex leverage from AI-driven network orchestration reducing OpEx by 5% in Wireless.

Key trends include our 5G SA core live in 20 metros, enabling network slicing for low-latency NovaStream 8K streaming and edge computing partnerships with AWS. In Wireline, Open RAN trials with Nokia and Samsung are on track to cut capex 15% by FY2026. U.S. remains 75% of revenue, with mature market growth shifting from volume to ARPU. Latin America accelerates to 12% revenue growth on 4G/5G upgrades, while Europe pilots via Vodafone JV add modest 5% growth but high-margin IoT revenue. Bundling has driven 28% household penetration, up from 22% last year, with 'Connex bundles'—broadband + NovaStream + mobile for $120/month—reducing overall churn to 1.1%. Risks include spectrum auction dynamics, regulatory scrutiny on price hikes, and content cost inflation, mitigated by our 40% in-house originals slate. This guidance assumes no material macroeconomic deterioration, stable capex at around 16% of revenue, and FCF conversion of 95% of EBITDA.

I'd also like to address what’s top of mind for our shareholders: the sustainability of our dividend and our broader commitment to delivering strong total shareholder returns. Our Board has today declared a quarterly dividend of $0.55 per share, or $2.20 annualized, marking the 17th consecutive year of increases. At today's closing price of $48.75, that translates to a forward yield of 4.5%, well above the S&P 500 Communications Services sector average of 2.8% and competitive with peers like Verizon at 6.8% and AT&T at around 5.2%. Over the past five years, we've grown the dividend at a CAGR of 8.2%, outpacing inflation and the 4-5% median for telco peers.

Sustainability—our payout ratio stands at a healthy 58% of adjusted EPS, which came in at $3.78 for the trailing 12 months, down slightly from 62% last year due to one-time integration costs from our European fiber JV. But the real story is free cash flow coverage, which is our north star. We generated $7.9 billion in levered FCF over the last four quarters—up 12% year-over-year—comfortably covering our $4.2 billion annual dividend obligation by a 1.9x multiple. This is ahead of the 1.5x coverage guideline we set in our 2022 capital markets day and stronger than Comcast's 1.7x or Charter's 1.4x.

Why the FCF strength? Our U.S. wireless segment—now 45% 5G SA coverage—saw ARPU expand 3.1% to $52.40, driven by premium unlimited plans bundled with NovaStream access. Postpaid churn held at a stellar 0.92%, below industry norms. Broadband added 450,000 fiber subs in Q4 alone, pushing penetration to 42% in our 15-state footprint, with 1 Gbps+ speeds fueling sticky gaming and remote work demand. Margins here expanded 220 basis points to 52% EBITDA, thanks to opex efficiencies from our AI-driven network orchestration platform across 70% of our edge nodes.

In North America, 68% of EBITDA, FCF margins hit 18%, bolstered by the FCC's C-band spectrum deployment—we've monetized 90% of our 3.7 GHz holdings via dynamic spectrum sharing. Europe, 22% of the mix via our Vodafone JV, faced headwinds from Ofcom's mid-band auction costs, capping ARPU growth at 1.8% in GBP terms, but our FWA initiative added €250 million in incremental FCF. Asia-Pacific, our 10% growth engine through StarHub partnerships in Singapore, delivered 25% FCF growth on 5G mmWave densification for enterprise private networks.

NovaStream hit 28 million global paid subs—up 14% YoY—closing the gap with Disney+ and Paramount+, with ARPU at $9.80 thanks to ad-supported tiers and live sports rights like our NBA package. Content capex is stabilizing at 14% of revenue, down from 18% peaks, as we leverage user-generated AI curation to boost engagement 22%.

On shareholder returns beyond the dividend: We've repurchased $2.1 billion in shares YTD at an average of $46.20, retiring 4.3% of float, with $4.8 billion remaining in our 2024 authorization. Combined, dividends plus buybacks delivered a trailing 12-month TSR yield of 8.7%—$4.2B dividends + $2.8B buybacks against a $52B market cap—outperforming the sector's 6.2%. Since our 2020 pandemic low, cumulative TSR stands at 145%, blending 42% stock appreciation with these returns.

Looking forward, sustainability is locked in. We guide to $8.5-9.0 billion in FY2025 FCF, implying 2.0-2.1x dividend coverage even after $3.2 billion in sustaining capex for 5G-Advanced and Open RAN trials. Leverage is down to 2.3x net debt-to-EBITDA from 2.8x at year-start, target 2.0x by 2026 via $1.5B annual delevering. Dividend growth? Expect 6-8% annually through the cycle, supported by 3-4% organic EBITDA growth from broadband ramps and media adjacencies like connected TV OS integrations. We're prioritizing FCF compounding over M&A froth, with initiatives like network slicing for 5G enterprise targeting $1B revenue by 2027 and edge computing partnerships with hyperscalers like AWS. In a high-interest world, our 4.5% yield with growth is a fortress balance sheet play. Our dividend isn't just sustainable—it's a growing engine for shareholder value creation, committed to 8-10% annual TSR.

For the full year 2023 equivalent in our FY2024 context, we generated $12.8 billion in free cash flow, marking a robust 17% year-over-year increase from $10.9 billion. In Q4 alone, we delivered $3.6 billion, surpassing our guidance midpoint and up 12% sequentially. Free cash flow, defined as adjusted operating cash flow minus capital expenditures, benefited from adjusted operating cash flow reaching a record $30.9 billion for the year, fueled by 4.2 million postpaid wireless net additions—our strongest in five years—driven by our 5G Ultra Wideband network covering 98% of North America with midband spectrum. This translated to a 3.1% increase in wireless service ARPU to $58.50, thanks to premium 5G plans bundled with NovaStream, which saw 15 million paid streaming subscribers, up 22% YoY, gaining share against Netflix and Disney+ through exclusive sports rights like our NFL Sunday Ticket partnership.

Broadband side, our fiber-to-the-home footprint expanded to 25 million locations passed, adding 1.1 million fiber net adds and boosting residential ARPU by 4% to $72. Media synergies from tuck-in acquisitions contributed $450 million in incremental cash flow through content licensing efficiencies and ad revenue growth, with our targeted addressable TV platform achieving a 25% YoY increase in CTV ad impressions.

Capex came in at $18.1 billion, or 14% of revenue, within guidance. We prioritized spectrum-efficient 5G SA core deployments, investing $4.2 billion in C-band and 3.45 GHz auctions, and $2.8 billion in Open RAN pilots with Nokia and Samsung to reduce vendor lock-in and long-term opex by 15-20%. Disciplined cost management—$1.2 billion in procurement savings via global supply chain optimization—kept capex flat YoY despite inflation.

North America drove 82% of our FCF at $10.5 billion, with high ARPU markets like the U.S. Northeast yielding $65 wireless ARPU amid low 0.78% postpaid churn. Europe contributed $1.6 billion, up 25% YoY from 5G roaming partnerships post Vodafone Iberia JV. In Latin America, via Claro Brazil, we generated $700 million, a 30% surge from 5G launches in São Paulo and Mexico City, capturing prepaid-to-postpaid upgrades at 18% penetration.

On utilization—our disciplined capital allocation framework prioritizes shareholder returns while fueling growth. Of the $12.8 billion generated: 45%, or $5.8 billion, went to dividends, including our 8th consecutive 7% increase in the quarterly dividend to $0.72 per share, yielding 3.8%—competitive with AT&T but with superior growth. 35%, or $4.5 billion, funded share repurchases under our $15 billion authorization, retiring 3.8% of shares and delivering $2.1 billion in EPS accretion, accretive given our 8.2% FCF yield versus Comcast's 7.1%. 15%, or $1.9 billion, reduced net debt by $1.4 billion net, bringing net leverage to 2.1x adjusted EBITDA—below our 2.5x target. The remaining 5%, or $600 million, supported strategic tuck-ins, including a $350 million stake in a 6G R&D consortium with Ericsson and a $250 million content deal for premium Korean dramas to bolster NovaStream in APAC.

Looking ahead, FY2025 FCF of $13.8 to $14.5 billion, implying 8-13% growth, driven by wireless equipment sales normalization, further fiber penetration to 30 million homes, and $800 million in additional opex savings from AI-driven network orchestration and edge computing. This positions us to accelerate buybacks to $6 billion while maintaining capex for 5G-Advanced upgrades. Our FCF engine underscores resilience amid spectrum costs and content competition, enabling outperformance like T-Mobile in wireless cash conversion at 48% of revenue while mirroring Comcast's media diversification.

Moving to cost of revenue, which came in at $4.25 billion for the quarter, up 6.2% year-over-year from $4.00 billion, but flat sequentially. As a percentage of total revenue, it held steady at 52.3%, a testament to disciplined cost management amid inflation in energy and labor, and upfront investments in next-gen infrastructure.

Network operations and access costs, 58% of CoR or $2.47 billion—up 8.1% YoY—driven by accelerated 5G SA rollout and Open RAN deployments. In the U.S., mirroring Verizon's C-Band strategy, we've deployed over 15,000 new 5G small cells, with leasing and backhaul up $120 million YoY due to fiber interconnectivity. Energy costs up 12% from diesel generator usage during peak loads. North America: 65% at $1.60 billion, reflecting 5G traffic from FWA at $75/month ARPU. EMEA up 10% to $520 million from network sharing with Vodafone and spectrum refarming. APAC flat at $350 million thanks to NFV/SDN efficiencies in India JV with Reliance Jio, slashing opex 18% per site.

Content and programming costs, 24% or $1.02 billion, up 2.8% YoY from renewals for Premier League and NBA, adding $80 million amortization. Offset by bundling, dipping content costs to 28% of video subs revenue. Ad-supported tiers at 35% of 45 million households helped. Europe up 5% to $280 million from local quotas; U.S. stabilized with in-house originals.

CPE and installation, 12% or $510 million, down 3.5% YoY from eSIM and self-install kits, cutting dispatches 22%. Deployed 2.1 million Wi-Fi 6E routers at $145/unit.

Other CoR, 6% or $255 million, up 9% on roaming surges, mitigated by Telefónica agreements.

Over the past year, CoR grew at 5.8% CAGR, but we've clawed back 220 bps margin expansion via AI routing reducing bandwidth costs 14% with Google Cloud, and edge transcoding. Gross margin at 47.7%, on track for 48.5%. For FY2025: Open RAN to 50% of sites for $300 million savings; content discipline via FAST; FWA in rural U.S. with BEAD; APAC mmWave for AR/VR.

Now, turning to our Enterprise and B2B growth initiatives, a cornerstone of our strategy. This segment represents our highest-margin opportunity, leveraging our fiber backbone, 5G edge, and media platform for hyperscalers, financials, retailers, and media enterprises. In Q4, revenues accelerated 28% year-over-year to $1.82 billion, outpacing company growth and now 42% of total service revenues—up from 35%. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to 52%, driven by scale in SDN-orchestrated networks and recurring managed services.

Progress and key wins: First, 5G Private Networks and Edge Computing—explosive demand for low-latency connectivity. Standout: $450 million, five-year contract with GlobalLogix for private 5G across 25 fulfillment centers, including slicing-as-a-service on CBRS, 99.9999% uptime, edge MEC for AI analytics. 60% complete, $90 million ARR, part of $2.1 billion pipeline up 40% QoQ.

Second, SD-WAN and SASE: $320 million deal with EuroBank Alliance for zero-trust overlays on 400G fiber, AI threat detection at 98% efficacy. EMEA B2B up 45% to $420 million, fueled by SecureNet Edge acquisition for $180 million.

Third, Media CDN: $280 million with StreamForge for ad insertion and 4K/8K ABR, QUIC HTTP/3 reducing buffering 40%. APAC up 55% to $310 million, Singtel partnerships, $150 million Alibaba Cloud gaming edge. Handling 15% regional OTT traffic.

Trends: Enterprise capex to 5G-advanced/Wi-Fi 7, ARPU up 22% to $1,450/site; CHIPS Act subsidies $500 million opportunities; AI edge with NVIDIA. Churn sub-1%, NPS 72. Pipeline $12.4 billion—65% contracted—positioning for 25-30% FY2025 growth. Investing $800 million in dark fiber and Open RAN, alliances with AWS and Azure. Enterprise B2B is transforming NovaTel into the intelligent edge backbone.

Before handing back, a deep dive into our spectrum portfolio, the lifeblood of wireless ops, powering 5G SA, FWA, and media delivery. As of Q4 FY2024, we hold 285 MHz average mid-band across 5G footprint—comparable to Verizon post-C-band, strong 160 MHz 2.5 GHz EBS. Plus 120 MHz low-band 600 MHz, 1.2 GHz mmWave urban. Overall utilization 82%—up from 68% YoY, 55% 2022—via 5G densification, DSS.

By band: Mid-band 87%, peak 92%, refarmed 40 MHz legacy for 200 MHz CA. Low-band 71%, 98% POP coverage for indoor streaming to 15 million SpectrumLink TV+ subs. mmWave 65% in 18,000 small cells, 2.5 Gbps speeds for private nets, Hollywood AR/VR pilot.

Gains from 22% spectral efficiency via ORAN massive MIMO from Nokia/Samsung, 12 ms median latency for cloud gaming, 5G multicast Release 17.

Regional: Northeast/California 91%, FWA 2.8 million households up 45%, mmWave 78% URLLC. Southeast/Texas 84%, mid-band for BEAD. Midwest/rural 72%, CBRS 70 MHz.

Allocation strategy: Repurposing 60 MHz 4G by mid-2025 for 1 Gbps; DSA 3.45-3.55 GHz pilot. Auctions: $2.5B for Auction 108 40-60 MHz; swaps like T-Mobile deal. C-band for D2D satellite.

Growth: 30% mid-band FWA to 5M subs 55% margin; 15% NaaS enterprise 500+ deployments; 10% edge caching/multicast saving 18% CDN for 50M streams; 20% wholesale $800M 40% margins.

Trajectory to 92% utilization by 2026 underpins 15-18% wireless EBITDA CAGR, ROIC >25%.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Mike. I'd like to provide an update on our network performance. We've made significant strides in expanding our 5G coverage and increasing network capacity. We're also investing in advanced technologies like network slicing and edge computing to support new applications and services. Our network uptime and reliability remain high at over 99.99%. We are also improving latency metrics through AI optimizations, now averaging 12 milliseconds in key markets.

David Kim: Thank you. We've seen strong customer growth and improved customer satisfaction scores this quarter, with NPS reaching 72. Our bundled service offerings are resonating well with customers, and we're focused on providing a seamless and personalized customer experience through Connex bundles. We are also focused on increasing enterprise penetration, where B2B now drives 42% of service revenue.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to enhance our network and services. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations and improve efficiency, including predictive maintenance and dynamic spectrum sharing. We are also working on developing new products and services that leverage 5G and edge computing, such as AR/VR metaverse and 6G R&D with Qualcomm. Our R&D efforts are concentrated on Open RAN for 50% adoption and 6G terahertz trials.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your plans for expanding your presence in the enterprise market and how you plan to compete with existing players, specifically regarding private 5G network deployments?

David Kim: Thanks, John. Our enterprise expansion is accelerating, as Mike highlighted, with Q4 B2B revenue up 28% to $1.82 billion. Key wins like the $450 million GlobalLogix private 5G deal across 25 sites demonstrate our slicing-as-a-service on CBRS, delivering 99.9999% uptime and edge integration. Our $2.1 billion pipeline, up 40%, positions us for 25-30% growth, competing via SDN scale, AI security, and media CDN synergies. Investments in dark fiber and Open RAN alliances with AWS ensure we lead in the edge economy.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for the impact of inflation and rising interest rates on your business, and how do you plan to mitigate those risks, especially regarding capex efficiency?

Mike Chen: Great question, Emily. Inflation at 2-3% is baked into our FY2025 guidance, with capex efficiency from Open RAN and AI supply chains keeping intensity at 15.5-16%. Rising rates favor our fortress balance sheet—2.1x leverage, $4.5B cash—enabling delevering and buybacks. Mitigation includes $1.2B procurement savings, 20% faster deployments, and FCF growth to $13.8-14.5B for 2x dividend coverage. We're resilient, prioritizing efficient growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Lee: Can you discuss your sustainability initiatives and your plans for reducing your carbon footprint, and how will you measure your success, specifically addressing energy cost trends in network ops?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Robert. Sustainability is core, with AI orchestration reducing energy 12-14% via traffic routing and edge processing. BEAD rural builds counter satellites efficiently, targeting 300-400 bps margin expansion. Success measured by downtime <0.01%, 42-43% EBITDA by FY2027, and ROIC >25% on greenfield fiber. Our 6G R&D includes low-power terahertz, aligning with EU Gigabit goals.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth. Thank you for your time and interest in NovaTel Communications.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
